description:
ZATCA wave 25: businesses in Saudi Arabia whose revenue subject to VAT went above SAR 187,500 in any year from 2022 to 2025 must integrate their e-invoicing with the Fatoora portal by 1 February 2027. In this video: what Phase 2 (the integration phase) means - clearance for standard B2B invoices, reporting within 24 hours for simplified invoices, the cryptographic stamp - who is in wave 25, and how to connect Zoho Books to Fatoora (OTP, CSID, Arabic fields, Push to Fatoora, statuses) step by step.

beats.text: Wave 25: integrate your e-invoicing with Fatoora by 1 February 2027

beats.label: VAT revenue in any year, 2022 to 2025

lines: On the twenty fourth of July 2026, Saudi Arabia's tax authority, ZATCA, announced wave twenty five of e-invoicing Phase 2.
It covers businesses whose revenue subject to VAT went above one hundred eighty seven thousand five hundred riyals, in any year from 2022 to 2025.
And their deadline to integrate is the first of February 2027.
In the next few minutes: what Phase 2 means, who is in, and how to connect Zoho Books to ZATCA's Fatoora portal, step by step, with the exact menu names.
Chapter one. What Phase 2 means.

beats.text: A scanned paper invoice does not count
Phase 2: your system talks to ZATCA

lines: Phase 1 started on the fourth of December 2021. From then on, invoices had to be created electronically.
And a paper invoice that you simply scan or copy into a file is not an electronic invoice.
Phase 2, the integration phase, goes one step further. It connects your invoicing system directly to ZATCA, so your invoices reach the authority electronically, through Fatoora.
It started on the first of January 2023, and ZATCA brings businesses in group by group, in waves.

beats.text: A cryptographic stamp on every invoice
A Phase 2 QR code on simplified invoices

lines: Here is the big change. A standard tax invoice, the business to business kind, must be cleared by ZATCA before you share it with your buyer.
A simplified invoice, the kind you give to consumers, must be reported to Fatoora within twenty four hours of issuing it.
Your software also adds a cryptographic stamp, so ZATCA can check where each invoice came from, and that nobody changed it.
And simplified invoices carry a new Phase 2 QR code, with nine pieces of data inside. The good news: your invoicing software does all of this for you.
So in practice, a business invoice now travels like this. You create it in your software, as usual.
The software stamps it and builds the electronic file, then sends it to ZATCA through Fatoora.
Only after ZATCA clears it, do you share it with your customer.
Chapter two. Wave twenty five. Are you in?
The first wave, in January 2023, was only for giants, with revenue above three billion riyals.
By February 2025, the line was down to seven million riyals.
Wave twenty four was for businesses above three hundred seventy five thousand riyals, with a deadline of the thirtieth of June 2026.
And wave twenty five halves that again, to one hundred eighty seven thousand five hundred riyals, with a deadline of the first of February 2027.

items.text: Wave 25: revenue subject to VAT above SAR 187,500 in 2022, 2023, 2024 or 2025
Integrate with Fatoora by no later than 1 February 2027

lines: These are ZATCA's own words from the announcement: revenue subject to VAT above one hundred eighty seven thousand five hundred riyals, during 2022, 2023, 2024 or 2025.
And integration with Fatoora by no later than the first of February 2027.

stats.label: one year over the line is enough

lines: The test is your revenue subject to VAT, above one hundred eighty seven thousand five hundred riyals.
If you crossed that line in just one of the years 2022, 2023, 2024 or 2025, you are in.
ZATCA says it tells each wave directly, at least six months before its integration date.
Here is a simple example. Say your shop sold more than the line in 2024.
But business was slower in 2025, and you stayed below it.
You are still in wave twenty five, because one year over the line is enough.
So look at your figures for those four years now, not in late January.
Not sure whether you are in? Talk to your tax adviser, and watch for ZATCA's notice, which comes at least six months before your date.
And if you use Zoho Books, the connection to Fatoora takes only a few steps. Let me show you.
Chapter three. Connect Zoho Books to Fatoora.

beats.text: 2. Your Saudi address complete in Zoho Books

lines: Before you start, have three things ready. First, access to your business account on ZATCA's Fatoora portal.
Second, your organisation's full Saudi address filled in, in Zoho Books. I'll show you exactly which fields in chapter four.
And third, ten quiet minutes, because the password you are about to create works for just one hour.

visual.title: Step 1: get a one-time password
steps: Log in with your ZATCA account
Enter 1 if Zoho Books is your only system

lines: First, log in to ZATCA's Fatoora portal, and choose Onboard New Solution Unit or Device.
Zoho says to enter one as the number of devices, if Zoho Books is your only invoicing system.
Then copy the one time password. It is valid for only one hour, so keep Zoho Books open. If the hour runs out, simply generate a new one.
Now open Zoho Books, and click the gear icon to open Settings.
The e-invoicing settings live under Taxes and Compliance.
Enter the one time password in Zoho Books within that hour, and it generates your C S I D, the cryptographic stamp identifier that links your system to ZATCA.

beats.text: Check: View List Of Solutions and Devices

lines: To check that it worked, go back to Fatoora, and open View List Of Solutions and Devices.
When the C S I D expires, renew it in Fatoora first, then click Renew C S I D on the same e-invoicing settings page in Zoho Books.
You set this up once, and you only come back here when the C S I D needs renewing.
Chapter four. Your data and your invoices.
Phase 2 invoices need a full Saudi address. In your organisation profile, fill in the building number and the additional number.
Plus the street, the district, the city and the postal code.
For customers, Zoho asks for the customer name and the billing address in Arabic.
Item names on the invoice must be in Arabic too.
And for standard business invoices, add the customer's national I D and full address. Zoho marks all of these as mandatory for e-invoicing.
To send an invoice to ZATCA, go to Sales, then Invoices, open the invoice, and click Push to Fatoora.
Push a standard invoice before you send it to the customer. Push a simplified invoice within twenty four hours of sending it.
The status moves from Yet to be Pushed, to Push Initiated, to Pushed. If it says Failed, fix the error and push again.

beats.text: Approvals on? Push waits for the last approver

lines: Once an invoice is pushed, Zoho Books keeps a P D F of it, with the X M L file attached.
If you use transaction approvals, the invoice is pushed only after the final approver approves it. So approve on time.
And when a customer approves a quote that turns into an invoice, the preference Create, Push and Send does the push for you.

beats.text: Drafts: you push each one yourself
Or: Create, Charge, Push and Send

lines: Recurring invoices have three choices. Create Invoices as Drafts means you push each one yourself.
Create, Push, and Send Invoices means Zoho pushes and sends them for you.
And Create, Charge, Push and Send also charges the customer first, then pushes and sends.
Finally, give the right people the Push Transactions permission, under Settings, then Roles.
So, a quick recap. Business invoices are cleared by ZATCA before you send them.
Consumer invoices are reported within twenty four hours.
And every invoice carries the cryptographic stamp, and simplified ones the Phase 2 QR code.
Chapter five. Your checklist.

visual.title: Before 1 February 2027
items: Generate the CSID in Zoho Books

lines: One. Check your revenue subject to VAT for 2022 to 2025.
Two. Get the one time password from Fatoora.
Three. Enter it in Zoho Books within the hour, to generate the C S I D.
Four. Fill in the Arabic names and the full address fields.
Five. Push your first invoice, and check that it says Pushed.

stats.label: OTP expires, get a new one

lines: Three easy mistakes to avoid. Waiting too long with the one time password. It expires after an hour, and then you need a new one.
Reporting simplified invoices late. You have twenty four hours.
And leaving failed invoices. Open them, fix the error, and push again the same day.
Do this early, and the first of February is just another working day.
Every invoice then goes to Fatoora straight from Zoho Books, with no extra work at month end.
